company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the robotics and Physical AI space.

MillerKnoll posted solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — clean EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, falling 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was held unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings CFO experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership transition event with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% well below the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft, with increasing material costs adding further gross margin pressure. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a surge of roughly 75% year-over-year in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout that validates the drug's competitive profile in the increasingly crowded weight-loss drug market. The strong efficacy data is a clear near-term positive catalyst for the stock.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the earnings rundown for Tuesday September 22nd. No broad macro commentary in today's note — this one is purely company-specific, so let's get right into it.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03. But here's the problem — the beat was low quality. It was driven by tariff refunds worth 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture gets uglier. Domestic comps missed significantly, up only 1.6% versus the Street's expectation of 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say sales linearity improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter, and they expressed confidence going into fiscal 2027 — but the core print is hard to get excited about.

Next up, Cognex. The machine vision company announced it's acquiring RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic move into robotics and Physical AI — directionally bullish for Cognex's positioning.

MillerKnoll posted a solid beat on fiscal Q1 earnings — 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents. And crucially, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, clean EPS of 42 cents still beat the 36-cent consensus. Sales were light, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Guidance is a slight mixed bag — the fiscal 2027 sales range was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance was left unchanged. Net net, a reasonably clean quarter.

THOR Industries disappointed. Fiscal Q4 earnings per share came in at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the 13.85% the Street was modeling. Management was candid about the challenges: stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are straining household budgets and keeping RV retail soft. They expect a relatively flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 and won't provide formal guidance until later this fall. There were some positives — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year. But the headline print and qualitative tone are cautious.

Finally, the big mover this morning — Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking in pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. That is a strong efficacy readout and a clear near-term catalyst. The GLP-1 space remains one of the hottest areas in biotech, and Viking just gave itself a meaningful seat at the table.

Bottom line for today: it's a mixed earnings tape. Viking is the standout mover to the upside. AutoZone and THOR are the stories where the headline numbers need closer scrutiny. Stay focused on the details.
